subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` config writes warn on unknown or pattern-like entries, fail closed, or remain audit-only for custom/plugin command IDs?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the permanent behavior affects a security knob and could block valid plugin/custom command IDs if implemented as hard validation.

options.title: Warn before write
options.body: Emit a non-blocking warning from config set/patch/unset validation for unknown or pattern-like deny entries and keep custom IDs writable.

options.title: Fail closed with plugin-aware registry
options.body: Reject unknown deny entries only after maintainers define a complete built-in plus plugin command registry and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep audit-only
options.body: Leave config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to report ineffective deny entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn before write
recommendation.body: Emit a non-blocking warning from config set/patch/unset validation for unknown or pattern-like deny entries and keep custom IDs writable.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to the security audit and gateway node policy history involved in this boundary.
